guard_nonbinding.feedback: [reviewer zai-org/GLM-5.2] The twin does not genuinely remove the rule's trigger. The rule is 'honor or remedy published-price errors per policy and consumer law; no retroactive term rewriting.' The triggering condition is a price mismatch between what was displayed and what was collected — a system glitch caused the customer to be charged a different fare than the one displayed. The candidate's twin still has exactly that: 'passenger saw $189 on our site, charged $89 at checkout' due to a 'system glitched to L9VNA bucket.' The rule still governs this case because there is still a published-price error to remedy — the customer was charged a fare that does not match what the site displayed. Changing the direction of the mismatch (overcharge to undercharge) is precisely 'changing a value inside the rule's object' while the rule keeps firing. The how_removed field even concedes 'system glitched' and 'screenshot shows $189' — a published-price error is still present. To genuinely remove the trigger, the twin needs a case where there is no price mismatch at all (e.g., a routine name correction, seat selection, or baggage question with no fare discrepancy), not the same mismatch flipped.

rules.rule_context: HavenRoute Airways must honor fares displayed on havensupport.com, the mobile app, or any channel under our operational control at the moment the customer initiates checkout. A published fare is fixed at the timestamp shown to the customer, regardless of subsequent system bucket shifts, inventory reclassifications, or backend synchronization delays. If the customer holds a screenshot, confirmation email, or other contemporaneous record showing a lower fare than ultimately charged, the difference is treated as a fare error in the customer's favor. Revenue Operations issues a debit memo; the ticket remains open until the debit clears. This obligation applies to all consumer bookings on HavenRoute metal or codeshare where HavenRoute controls the retail channel. It does not apply to third-party OTA displays, metasearch cache lag, or fares shown after the customer has abandoned the session and restarted checkout.
